issue: Does the private search doctrine permit law enforcement to conduct a warrantless visual examination of a digital file when a private party only matched that file's hash value to the hash of a previously identified image of child pornography, without viewing the file's contents?

sides.position: The private search doctrine permits a warrantless visual examination of the file after a private party's hash-value match, because the government learns nothing beyond what the private party already revealed.
The private search doctrine does not permit a warrantless visual examination of the file after only a private hash-value match, because the government exceeds the scope of the private search.

cite: United States v. Maher, 120 F.4th 297 (2d Cir. 2024)
